learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of automation and control methods.
Analyze and design continuous-time control systems, from the classical theory of linear systems control approach.
Automate simple industrial processes using programmable logic controllers.
Understand the fundamentals of industrial communications.

syllabus_topics: Topic I. Fundamentals of automatic regulation
Topic III. Analysis of control systems in the time domain.
Analysis of systems using the Root Locus.
Topic IV. Design of regulation systems
Design of regulators using the Root Locus.
Topic V. Analysis of control systems in the frequency domain
Stability, phase margin, and gain margin.
Block B: Industrial Instrumentation and Automation
teaching_methods: Theoretical lectures with active student participation
Self-assessment tests through the Virtual Classroom
Experimental and/or technological laboratories (model and control of real systems, automation of digital twins with Matlab/Simulink)
Lectures and resolution of key representative problems
Flipped classroom, constructivist, and participatory methodology
assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted average of four components: a mid-term written test (20%), practical work grade (15%), self-assessment tests (5%), and a final written test (60%). A minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for the final written test to be included in the average. If the overall average is greater than 5 but the final written test is below 5, the final grade will be 4.5. For the extraordinary evaluation, only the final written test (60%) can be re-taken, maintaining the scores from the other components. A minimum of 5 out of 10 is also required for the re-taken final written test.
